Combine and scale sankey data from multiple receivers

Source: R/export.R
combine_sankey_data.Rd

Combines per-receiver data.frames from prepare_for_ccflowr(), applies global min-max scaling, maps ccflowR-compatible columns, and optionally filters by a quantile threshold.

combine_sankey_data(..., threshold_quantile = 0.95)

Arguments

...

One or more data.frames returned by prepare_for_ccflowr(), or a single list of such data.frames.

threshold_quantile

Quantile threshold for filtering rows (default: 0.95). Set to 0 to skip thresholding and return all rows with scaled columns.

Value

A data.frame with 10 columns: the 6 raw columns from prepare_for_ccflowr() plus 4 scaled columns:

sender

Sender cell type

ligand

Ligand gene name

receptor

Receptor gene name

receiver

Receiver cell type

weighted_score

Raw combined score per sender

weight

L-R interaction weight from signaling network

scaled_weighted_score

Global min-max scaled weighted_score

scaled_activity

Same as scaled_weighted_score (ccflowR compat)

scaled_ligand_expression

Same as scaled_weighted_score (ccflowR compat)

scaled_receptor_expression

Min-max scaled L-R weight (ccflowR compat)

Details

This function encapsulates the combine-rescale-threshold pattern that is needed when analyzing multiple receiver cell types. Each call to prepare_for_ccflowr() produces per-receiver raw scores; combine_sankey_data() then:

  1. Combines all inputs via rbind()

  2. Applies global min-max scaling to weighted_score

  3. Maps ccflowR-compatible column aliases

  4. Filters to rows at or above the threshold_quantile

Only applicable to NicheNet framework results. MultiNicheNet produces different columns and does not participate in this workflow.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Prepare per-receiver data
data_basal <- prepare_for_ccflowr(result_basal, seurat_obj, network)
data_parabasal <- prepare_for_ccflowr(result_parabasal, seurat_obj, network)
data_suprabasal <- prepare_for_ccflowr(result_suprabasal, seurat_obj, network)

# Combine, scale globally, and threshold at 95th percentile
sankey_data <- combine_sankey_data(
    data_basal, data_parabasal, data_suprabasal,
    threshold_quantile = 0.95
)

# Or get all data without thresholding
full_data <- combine_sankey_data(
    data_basal, data_parabasal, data_suprabasal,
    threshold_quantile = 0
)

# Also accepts a list
sankey_data <- combine_sankey_data(
    list(data_basal, data_parabasal),
    threshold_quantile = 0.95
)
} # }
